plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and there's no benefit to bidding above or below my true value. Bidding my true value ($34) is the dominant strategy - if I win, I pay less than my value (profit); if I bid higher, I risk overpaying; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a single round with no repeated interaction to exploit, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit price is determined by my own sealed bid. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, my dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value ($28). Bidding higher risks overpaying (winning at a price above my value), while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, regardless of the ascending clock mechanic. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since it maximizes expected profit without risk of overpaying or losing value from underbidding. My value is $14, so I will bid exactly that.
